Workflow documentation

EVD n8n workflows

What each n8n workflow behind EVD's day-to-day automations does, what triggers it, which credentials it uses and where it is fragile. Generated from the workflow exports and their companion notes. Webhook endpoints are documented in the API reference.

CLEV 7

Crear menú reportes CLEV

Hook

Regenerates the numbered menu of HighLevel pipelines that people choose from when they ask for a report. It lists the current pipelines, numbers them, and writes the menu text and the list of valid numbers into two HighLevel custom values.

Get Highlevel pipeline stages

Sub

Returns every stage of every HighLevel opportunity pipeline, with its id, name and position. It is a sub-workflow: other workflows call it, it has no webhook or schedule.

Get Highlevel pipelines names and ids

Sub

Returns the id and name of every HighLevel opportunity pipeline. It is a sub-workflow: other workflows call it, it has no webhook or schedule.

Get menu from CRM

Sub

Reads the report menu stored in HighLevel and returns it as rows of number and pipeline name. It is a sub-workflow: other workflows call it, it has no webhook or schedule.

Informe de oportunidades CLEV v2.1

Hook

Builds a report of HighLevel opportunities, counted by pipeline, stage and contact type, and posts it as a message in Basecamp. It is called over a webhook with the number of the pipeline the requester picked from a menu, and afterwards stores the link to the Basecamp message back in HighLevel.

Notificación de errores

Err

Sends an email whenever another workflow fails. It is the shared error handler for the CLEV reporting workflows, not something that is called directly. A separate workflow with the same name does the same job for the Google Workspace workflows.

Webhook test

Hook

A two-node test workflow: a webhook followed by a wait. It does nothing else and looks like a leftover from trying out webhook authentication, but it is published, so its endpoint is live.

Google Workspace 7

Actualizar tabla cuentas delegadas

Hook Cron

Keeps the n8n data table Cuentas delegadas in step with the real Gmail delegations. For every mailbox in the /Cuentas Delegadas organisational unit it reads who the delegates are, then adds the missing rows to the table and deletes the stale ones.

Cambio email-nombre

Hook

Changes a Google Workspace user's primary email address and, optionally, their first and last name. It is called over a webhook, answers the caller as soon as the email has changed, and then removes the alias Google leaves behind on the old address.

Notificación de errores

Err

Sends an email whenever another workflow fails. It is the shared error handler for the EVD workflows, not something that is called directly.

Reporte Validación Usuarios Activos v 1.1

Cron

Emails a CSV of active Google Workspace accounts that are not enrolled in 2-step verification. It runs on a schedule twice a week.

Reporte Validación Usuarios Totales v 1

Hook

Builds an Excel file of every Google Workspace user, with their groups and delegated mailboxes, and emails it. It runs when its webhook is called.

Suspender cuenta Workspace v1.0

Hook

Suspends a Google Workspace user account. It is called over a webhook with the user's email address.

Workspaces User Discovery v1.4

Hook

Returns what a Google Workspace user has and belongs to: basic account details and, on request, admin details, shared drives, groups, delegated mailboxes, Chat spaces and Drive files. It is called over a webhook and answers with one combined object.

HighLevel 10

Actualizar campo Comunidad WhatsApp auto COL

Hook

Keeps a HighLevel contact field in step with membership of the Colombia WhatsApp announcements group. When someone joins or leaves the group, it finds the matching contact in the Colombia HighLevel account by phone number and sets the "Grupo de avisos WhatsApp" custom field to Ingresado or Retirado.

Actualizar tabla cache custom fields highlevel

Cron

Rebuilds the n8n data table CustomFieldsHighLevel, a cache of every custom field in every HighLevel account. For each account it fetches the custom fields, then replaces the table's contents with the fresh list.

Actualizar tabla cache iniciados - iniciado actualizado desde PI

Hook

Refreshes one person's row in the n8n data table Cache contactos Iniciados SKY when their contact changes in the Iniciados HighLevel account. HighLevel calls the webhook, the workflow reads the contact back from HighLevel and overwrites the cached row.

Copia contacto CRM a teléfono

Hook

A single webhook node with nothing connected after it. The name says it should copy a CRM contact to a phone, but no such logic exists: the endpoint accepts a call and does nothing.

Notificación de errores

Err

Sends an email whenever another workflow fails. It is the shared error handler for the HighLevel workflows, not something that is called directly. Separate workflows with the same name do the same job for the Google Workspace and CLEV areas.

Search contact email multi credential

Sub

Looks up a contact by email in one sede's HighLevel account. It is a sub-workflow: other workflows call it, it has no webhook or schedule. Only the Colombia branch is built.

Sub. Search all contacts by Sede Location ID multi credential

Sub

Returns every contact of one sede's HighLevel account. It is a sub-workflow: other workflows call it, it has no webhook or schedule. Only the Argentina and Chile branches are active.

Sub. Upsert contact by email multi credential Iniciados Sedes

Sub

Creates or updates one contact in a sede's HighLevel account, matched by email, and sets its "iniciado" custom fields. It is a sub-workflow: other workflows call it, it has no webhook or schedule.

test webhook events Iniciados

Hook

A single webhook node with nothing connected after it. It looks like a test endpoint for receiving events from the Iniciados HighLevel account: calls are accepted and can be inspected in n8n's execution log, but nothing is done with them.

Upsert Contacts from Iniciados to Sedes

Cron

Copies the "iniciados" from the cache table into HighLevel: every cached person is upserted into the Global account and, through a sub-workflow, into the account of their sede. It runs on a schedule.

CLEV Webhook

Crear menú reportes CLEV

Regenerates the numbered menu of HighLevel pipelines that people choose from when they ask for a report. It lists the current pipelines, numbers them, and writes the menu text and the list of valid numbers into two HighLevel custom values.

Trigger What it does Credentials Tricky nodes Who uses it

Trigger

POST /webhook/clev/create-menu on the n8n instance (Webhook node, path /clev/create-menu).

Authentication is header auth, using the credential Header Auth new auto@clev.org.

No responseMode is set, so n8n answers immediately and the menu is rebuilt afterwards. The response carries a Content-Type: application/json header.

When clicking ‘Execute workflow’ is also on the canvas but is disabled.

Request body

None. The workflow reads no request parameters.

What it does

  1. List the pipelines. Get Pipelines1 calls GET https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/opportunities/pipelines; split pipelines1 and split Pipeline ids names1 reduce each pipeline to id, name and dateAdded.
  2. Drop retired pipelines. Descartar OLD discards pipelines with "old" in their name (case-insensitive).
  3. Number them. Sort orders the rest by dateAdded, newest first, and Add index numbers them from 1.
  4. Find the two custom values. Get Custom Values reads HighLevel's custom values once, and Switch routes the one keyed numeros_reportes_automaticos to its first output and the one keyed menu_reportes_automaticos to its second.
  5. Write the valid numbers. Edit Fields builds 0,1,2,… and Update custom_values.numeros_reportes_automaticos field saves it with a PUT.
  6. Write the menu text. Edit Fields1 builds _*(0)*_ Todos _*| (1)*_ {name} _*| (2)*_ {name} … and Update custom_values.menu_reportes_automaticos saves it with a PUT.

Responses

Situation What the caller gets
Any call with valid auth n8n's immediate "workflow started" response. It says nothing about whether the menu was updated.

Credentials

Credential Type ID Used by
Header Auth new auto@clev.org httpHeaderAuth l03Uxy1XYUmnJuAk Webhook

The four HighLevel HTTP nodes (Get Pipelines1, Get Custom Values and the two Update custom_values… nodes) do not use a credential: they carry the HighLevel private integration token directly in an Authorization header parameter. In this repo's JSON the token is replaced with REDACTED_HIGHLEVEL_PRIVATE_INTEGRATION_TOKEN.

Failed executions are reported by Notificación de errores (ID bPvIORzqZ5PzAIRx), set as this workflow's error workflow in n8n.

Tricky nodes

  • Switch compares against HighLevel's own key syntax. The right-hand values {{ custom_values.numeros_reportes_automaticos }} and {{ custom_values.menu_reportes_automaticos }} look like n8n expressions but are plain text: that is how HighLevel writes a custom value's fieldKey.
  • The menu text is the contract with the report workflow. Get menu from CRM parses this exact format back into numbers and names, and Informe de oportunidades CLEV v2.1 matches the names against live pipelines. Changing the format in Edit Fields1 breaks both. The _*…*_ markers are chat-style bold/italic markup.
  • Numbers follow creation date, not a fixed order. Adding a pipeline makes it number 1 and shifts every other number, so the menu must be regenerated whenever pipelines change.
  • Edit Fields and Edit Fields1 run once (executeOnce) and read every row of Add index through $items("Add index").
  • Descartar OLD uses its false branch. The true output (names containing "old") is not connected.
  • The leading slash in the webhook path (/clev/create-menu) is part of the node's setting.

Who uses it

Not recorded in the workflow. Its output is read by Get menu from CRM and, through it, by Informe de oportunidades CLEV v2.1. To be filled in: who or what calls the webhook when pipelines change.

Get Highlevel pipeline stages

            
Returns every stage of every HighLevel opportunity pipeline, with its id, name and position. It is a sub-workflow: other workflows call it, it has no webhook or schedule.

          


          

            

              

                Trigger
                What it does
                Credentials

Trigger


Start (Execute Workflow Trigger, input passed through). It runs when another workflow calls it; at import the only caller is Informe de oportunidades CLEV v2.1, through its Call Get pipeline stages node.


What it does


    

  1. List the pipelines. Get Pipelines1 calls GET https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/opportunities/pipelines for the CLEV location.
    2. 

  2. Flatten to stages. split pipelines1 produces one item per pipeline and split Stages one item per stage.
    3. 

  3. Return. Return keeps id, position and name for each stage.
    4. 



Credentials


None. Get Pipelines1 carries the HighLevel private integration token directly in an Authorization header parameter. In this repo's JSON the token is replaced with REDACTED_HIGHLEVEL_PRIVATE_INTEGRATION_TOKEN.


Failed executions are reported by Notificación de errores (ID bPvIORzqZ5PzAIRx), set as this workflow's error workflow in n8n.


Tricky nodes


    

  • The output does not say which pipeline a stage belongs to. Only the stage's own id, position and name are returned; the caller matches stages by id.
    • 

  • Return writes position as a string. The caller converts it back to a number in its own mapping.
    • 

  • Get Pipelines1 runs once per incoming item, because the trigger passes its input through.
    • 

  • Stages of "old" pipelines are included.
    • 



Who uses it

Trigger


Start (Execute Workflow Trigger, input passed through). It runs when another workflow calls it; at import the only caller is Informe de oportunidades CLEV v2.1, through its Call Get Highlevel pipelines names and ids node.


What it does


    

  1. List the pipelines. Get Pipelines1 calls GET https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/opportunities/pipelines for the CLEV location.

  2. Flatten. split pipelines1 produces one item per pipeline, and split Pipeline ids names keeps only id and name.

Get menu from CRM

            
Reads the report menu stored in HighLevel and returns it as rows of number and pipeline name. It is a sub-workflow: other workflows call it, it has no webhook or schedule.

          


          

            

              

                Trigger
                What it does

Trigger


Start (Execute Workflow Trigger). It runs when another workflow calls it; at import the only caller is Informe de oportunidades CLEV v2.1, through its Call Get menu from crm node.


It declares one input, body_customData_selection_toNumber, which nothing in the workflow reads.


What it does


    

  1. Read the custom values. Get Custom Values calls GET https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/locations/{location}/customValues, and Split Out3 produces one item per custom value.
    2. 

  2. Pick the menu. seleccionar campo con menú en el CRM keeps the custom value keyed menu_reportes_automaticos.
    3. 

  3. Parse it. Generate table Indexes and pipelines names reads the menu text, finds every (number) marker and returns one item per entry with index and name.
    4. 



Credentials


None. Get Custom Values carries the HighLevel private integration token directly in an Authorization header parameter. In this repo's JSON the token is replaced with REDACTED_HIGHLEVEL_PRIVATE_INTEGRATION_TOKEN.


Failed executions are reported by Notificación de errores (ID bPvIORzqZ5PzAIRx), set as this workflow's error workflow in n8n.


Tricky nodes


    

  • Generate table Indexes and pipelines names depends on the menu's exact format. It expects the text written by Crear menú reportes CLEV (_*(0)*_ Todos _*| (1)*_ {name} …): a name is whatever sits between one (number) and the next, with surrounding spaces, underscores, asterisks and pipes stripped. A pipeline name containing a number in parentheses would be split in two.
    • 

  • seleccionar campo con menú en el CRM compares against HighLevel's key syntax. The right-hand value {{ custom_values.menu_reportes_automaticos }} is plain text, not an n8n expression.
    • 

  • The declared input is unused, and the caller passes nothing for it.
    •

Informe de oportunidades CLEV v2.1

            
Builds a report of HighLevel opportunities, counted by pipeline, stage and contact type, and posts it as a message in Basecamp. It is called over a webhook with the number of the pipeline the requester picked from a menu, and afterwards stores the link to the Basecamp message back in HighLevel.

          


          

            

              

                Trigger
                What it does
                Credentials
                Tricky nodes
                Who uses it
              

              

                


Draft note. At import the editor showed unpublished changes (draft last saved 2026-08-27, published version from 2026-08-13). A comparison of the two versions in n8n found no difference in nodes, connections or canvas positions, so this JSON behaves like the published version.




Trigger


POST /webhook/clev/reporte on the n8n instance (Webhook generación reporte node, path clev/reporte).


Authentication is header auth, using the credential Header Auth new auto@clev.org.


The webhook answers when the workflow has finished, with no body (responseMode: lastNode, responseData: noData).


When clicking ‘Execute workflow’ is also on the canvas but is disabled.


Request body


The body schema is not declared in the workflow; this is inferred from the expressions that read body.*. The sample payload kept on the canvas shows the caller is a HighLevel workflow, which sends the whole contact record; only these fields are read.






Field
Required
Used for





customData.selection
Yes
Number of the menu entry the requester chose. 0 means all pipelines; any other number is a pipeline's position in the menu stored in HighLevel.




full_name
No
Name of the requester, printed at the end of the report ("Reporte solicitado por").





What it does


    

  1. Read the selection. Extract menu selection and Menu Selection Number turn customData.selection into the number menuSelection.
    2. 

  2. Resolve the selection to a pipeline. Call Get menu from crm runs the sub-workflow Get menu from CRM, which returns the stored menu as rows of index and name. Filter menu selection keeps the row whose index equals menuSelection.
    3. 

  3. List the pipelines. Call Get Highlevel pipelines names and ids runs the sub-workflow of that name, and Not contain old drops pipelines with "old" in their name. If selection is todos 0 then either keeps all of them (selection 0) or, through Filter, only the pipeline whose name matches the selected menu row.
    4. 

  4. Fetch the opportunities. Get opportunities from menu pipelines calls GET https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/opportunities/search once per pipeline. Split opportunities and Opportunities reduce each opportunity to its ids and status.
    5. 

  5. Build the lookup tables, in parallel with steps 2–4:
      

    • Mappings Pipelines: pipeline id → pipeline name.
      • 

    • Call Get pipeline stages (sub-workflow Get Highlevel pipeline stages) → Mappings Stages (stage id → stage name) and Mappings Posición (stage id → position).
      • 

    • Search Iniciados searches HighLevel contacts whose tipo is Iniciado, Iniciado Ashram, Instructor Shakti Yoga or Swami, 500 per page; Mappings iniciados maps each of those contact ids to IN.
      • 

    • Create Mapping table appends the three tables into one.
      • 

    

    6. 

  6. Translate ids into names. ApplyMap adds Secuencia (pipeline name), Etapa (stage name) and Tipo (IN for the contacts found in step 5, PG for everyone else) to each opportunity.
    7. 

  7. Count. Remove empty drops blank items, Summarize counts opportunities per Secuencia, Etapa, Tipo and stage, ApplyMap2 adds the stage position, and Sort, Sort1, Sort2 order the rows by type, stage position and pipeline.
    8. 

  8. Write the report. Generate HTML text builds the HTML: one block per pipeline with its total and one line per stage ("stage: total (n IN / n PG)"), a grand total, and the requester's name.
    9. 

  9. Post it. Merge attaches the selected menu row, and Create a message posts the report to a Basecamp message board with the subject Reporte automático - {pipeline or "Todos"} - Corte {date}.
    10. 

  10. Store the link. Get Custom Values reads HighLevel's custom values, Filter1 picks the one whose key contains custom_values.link_reporte_basecamp, and the last node (Update custom_values.link_reporte_basecamp_no_editar__generado_automticamente) writes the Basecamp message URL into it.
    11. 



Responses






Situation
What the caller gets





Report posted
An empty response, once the Basecamp message exists and the link has been stored.




Any step fails
n8n's error response; the failure is also emailed by Notificación de errores.

Three HTTP nodes do not use a credential: Search Iniciados, Get Custom Values and the final Update custom_values… node carry the HighLevel private integration token directly in an Authorization header parameter. In this repo's JSON the token is replaced with REDACTED_HIGHLEVEL_PRIVATE_INTEGRATION_TOKEN.


It calls three sub-workflows: Get menu from CRM, Get Highlevel pipelines names and ids and Get Highlevel pipeline stages.


It needs three community nodes installed on the instance: n8n-nodes-applymap (ApplyMap, ApplyMap1, ApplyMap2), n8n-nodes-basecamp (Create a message) and n8n-nodes-highlevelv2.


Failed executions are reported by Notificación de errores (ID bPvIORzqZ5PzAIRx), set as this workflow's error workflow in n8n.


Tricky nodes


    

  • If empty always takes its false branch. Its condition tests the constant false, so Update Perdida opportunity to Stage Descartados1 never runs. The canvas is wired to move lost opportunities into the "Descartado" stage, but that update is switched off this way; lost opportunities only pass through Split opportunities1 → Opportunities1 → ApplyMap1 before being merged back in.
    • 

  • Split opportunities1 splits a field named opportunity, which the items reaching it do not have. With alwaysOutputData on, that path appears to produce blank items, which Remove empty then discards. If so, opportunities that are not open and not already in "Descartado" are left out of the count. Not verified against an execution.
    • 

  • Get opportunities from menu pipelines does not paginate. It makes one request per pipeline with no page or limit parameter, so a pipeline with more opportunities than HighLevel returns in one page would be under-counted. Not verified. Its Version  header also has a trailing space in the name.
    • 

  • The menu and the pipelines are matched by name. The selected number is resolved through the menu text stored in HighLevel (written by Crear menú reportes CLEV), then matched to a pipeline by exact name in Filter. A pipeline renamed or added after the menu was last generated will not match until the menu is regenerated.
    • 

  • ApplyMap nodes are a community node that looks values up in the table arriving on their second input. Tipo defaults to PG and unknown pipelines or stages to ND.
    • 

  • Generate HTML text formats the date in UTC-5 (Etc/GMT+5), regardless of the instance timezone.
    • 

  • Sticky Note holds a full sample webhook payload. It shows what HighLevel sends: the request headers and the whole contact record. In n8n it contains a real person's details and the webhook secret; in this repo's JSON those values are replaced with <redacted> and the rest of the note is unchanged.
    • 

  • Sticky Note1 is a to-do: move the HighLevel authentication from OAuth2 to the private integration token. The HTTP nodes already use the token; the OAuth2 credential remains only on the node that never runs.
    • 



Who uses it


CLEV staff, through HighLevel: a HighLevel workflow calls the webhook with the menu number a person chose, and the report appears in Basecamp. Which HighLevel workflow and which Basecamp project are not named in the export (the Basecamp bucket is 44535649, message board 9215268341). To be filled in.

Notificación de errores

            
Sends an email whenever another workflow fails. It is the shared error handler for the CLEV reporting workflows, not something that is called directly. Trigger


Error Trigger. n8n runs this workflow when a workflow that names it as its error workflow fails.


At import, six published workflows had it set as their error workflow in their n8n settings: Informe de oportunidades CLEV v2.1, Crear menú reportes CLEV, Get menu from CRM, Get Highlevel pipelines names and ids, Get Highlevel pipeline stages and Webhook test. That setting lives in each workflow's settings, which a clipboard export does not include.


What it does


    

  1. Error Trigger receives the failed execution's details.
    2. 

  2. Send email sends a plain-text email from auto@clev.org to servidores@evdsky.com with the subject Error en workflow n8n: {workflow name}. The body lists the workflow name, execution URL, last node executed, execution mode, execution ID, error message and stack trace.
    3.

Actualizar tabla cuentas delegadas

            
Keeps the n8n data table Cuentas delegadas in step with the real Gmail delegations. For every mailbox in the /Cuentas Delegadas organisational unit it reads who the delegates are, then adds the missing rows to the table and deletes the stale ones.

          


          

            

              

                Trigger
                What it does
                Credentials
                Tricky nodes
                Who uses it
              

              

                
Trigger


    

  • Schedule Trigger: the rule is left at its defaults (interval: [{}]), which in n8n means once a day at midnight, in the instance's timezone.
    • 

  • Webhook: GET /webhook/ee552566-6908-40e1-a58f-a496562425ce (no httpMethod is set, so n8n's default GET applies). Header auth with the credential Header Auth Bearer token n8n.workspace. No responseMode is set, so n8n answers immediately and the sync runs afterwards.
    • 

  • When clicking ‘Execute workflow’: manual run from the editor.
    • 



Request body


None. The workflow reads no request parameters.


What it does


    

  1. List the delegated mailboxes. Get users from OU Cuentas Delegadas lists the primaryEmail of every user where orgUnitPath='/Cuentas Delegadas' (retries once after 2 s).
    2. 

  2. Read each mailbox's delegates. Set impersonate email for service account credential puts the mailbox address in impersonate_email, and Get Gmail delegates calls GET https://gmail.googleapis.com/gmail/v1/users/{mailbox}/settings/delegates.
    3. 

  3. Flatten. Split Out produces one item per delegate and Edit Fields reduces it to email (the mailbox) and delegateEmail.
    4. 

  4. Read the current table. In parallel, Get row(s) reads every row of Cuentas delegadas.
    5. 

  5. Compare. To insert keeps the pairs found in Gmail but not in the table. To delete keeps the table rows no longer found in Gmail. Both match on email and delegateEmail.
    6. 

  6. Apply. If → Insert row adds the new pairs. If1 → Delete row(s) removes the stale rows by id.
    7. 

  7. Summarise. Aggregate and Aggregate1 collect the results into rowsAdded and rowsDeleted. Nothing reads them afterwards.
    8.

Tricky nodes


    

  • Get Gmail delegates — a failed read can look like "no delegates". The node has neverError on, so an API error for a mailbox returns a body without delegates instead of failing. Those mailboxes then contribute nothing, and To delete treats their existing table rows as stale. An outage on the Gmail API could therefore empty the table.
    • 

  • Set impersonate email for service account credential — the field name matters. The service account credential has to act as each mailbox to read its settings. The node name says the credential picks the address up from impersonate_email; the credential's own configuration is not part of the export, so this is not confirmed here.
    • 

  • To insert and To delete are the same Merge configured in opposite directions. Both use keepNonMatches; To insert outputs from input 1 (Gmail) and To delete from input 2 (the table). The input order on the canvas is what makes it correct.
    • 

  • If / If1 test for an empty item, not an empty list. The merges have alwaysOutputData on, so "nothing to do" arrives as one empty item. The check is "the first item has at least one key".
    • 

  • Delete row(s) has no column name in its filter. The condition only carries the value $json.id; it relies on the node's default key.
    • 

  • Get row(s) runs once (executeOnce), whichever trigger started the run.
    • 

  • Get users from OU Cuentas Delegadas error output is not connected. A failed listing ends the run without changes and without an error notification.
    • 

  • The webhook path is a generated UUID, unlike the readable paths on the other workflows.
    • 



Who uses it


No person calls it in normal operation; it runs on its schedule. Its output, the Cuentas delegadas table, is read by Workspaces User Discovery v1.4 and Reporte Validación Usuarios Totales v 1.

Cambio email-nombre

            
Changes a Google Workspace user's primary email address and, optionally, their first and last name. It is called over a webhook, answers the caller as soon as the email has changed, and then removes the alias Google leaves behind on the old address.

          


          

            

              

                Trigger
                What it does
                Credentials
                Tricky nodes
                Who uses it
              

              

                


Draft note. At import the editor showed unpublished changes (draft last saved 2026-09-23, published version from 2026-01-31). The JSON in this folder and this document are the published (live) version, 2908b6ab-93ef-4993-b79a-9f6b3948fe15, taken from n8n's API instead of the canvas. The unpublished draft differs in two places:


    

  • Webhook path: the draft renames 5cb58ab5-2ee7-4020-be98-0ac665e594d1 to workspace/user/nameupdate.
    • 

  • Edit Fields message: the draft starts "ambio exitoso" (missing C) instead of "Cambio exitoso".
    • 





Trigger


POST /webhook/5cb58ab5-2ee7-4020-be98-0ac665e594d1 on the n8n instance (Webhook node, published path 5cb58ab5-2ee7-4020-be98-0ac665e594d1).


Authentication is header auth, using the credential Header Auth Bearer token n8n.workspace.


The response is produced by the Respond to Webhook node (responseMode: responseNode), not by the end of the workflow.


Request body


The body schema is not declared in the workflow; this is inferred from the expressions that read $json.body.*.






Field
Required
Used for





correo
Yes
Current primary email of the user. Must look like an email and its domain must be in the Authorized domains data table.




correoNuevo
Yes, in practice
New primary email. A call without it ends in an error, after any name change has already been applied.




nombreNuevo
No
New first name. Skipped when empty.




ApellidoNuevo
No
New last name. Skipped when empty. Note the capital A.





What it does


    

  1. Pre-validation. Body parameters pre-validation checks correo against an email regex. Get row(s) then looks up the domain of correo in the Authorized domains data table, and If valid domains passes only if a row came back. Either failure goes to Prevalidation fails. Error message and the workflow ends there.
    2. 

  2. Look up the user. get User details fetches the user by correo from Google Workspace (retries once after 2 s). If the lookup fails, the workflow ends in Not found field false and debug info or Not found field Return message-1.
    3. 

  3. Change the first name. If checks nombreNuevo is not empty; if so Cambier Nombre updates firstName.
    4. 

  4. Change the last name. If1 checks ApellidoNuevo is not empty; if so Cambier Apellido updates lastName.
    5. 

  5. Change the email. Cambiar email sets primaryEmail to correoNuevo. This step always runs.
    6. 

  6. Verify. If3 compares the primaryEmail Google returned with correoNuevo. If they differ, Stop and Error fails the execution with "Error, no se cambió la dirección de correo".
    7. 

  7. Respond. Edit Fields adds a message field to the updated user object and Respond to Webhook returns it to the caller.
    8. 

  8. Clean up, after the response. Wait pauses 60 (seconds, per the message returned to the caller), then HTTP Request sends DELETE https://admin.googleapis.com/admin/directory/v1/users/{new email}/aliases/{old email} to remove the old address as an alias. Get a user then re-reads the user by correoNuevo; nothing consumes its output.
    9. 



Responses






Situation
What the caller gets





Email changed
The updated Google Workspace user object plus message (first incoming item of Respond to Webhook).




Validation failed, or user lookup failed
No Respond to Webhook node runs, so n8n sends its default response for a finished workflow. The error, not_found and debug.* fields built by the Set nodes are not returned.




Email did not change
n8n's error response, because Stop and Error fails the execution before any response is sent.

Tricky nodes


    

  • Cambiar email / If3 — correoNuevo is effectively mandatory. The email update is not guarded by an If, unlike the name updates. A call that only wants to change a name still reaches Cambiar email with an empty correoNuevo, then fails at If3. By that point the name changes from steps 3–4 have already been applied, so the caller sees an error for a call that partly succeeded.
    • 

  • Error branches never reach the caller. Prevalidation fails. Error message, Not found field false and debug info and Not found field Return message-1 are dead ends with no Respond to Webhook after them. Their output is only visible in the n8n execution log.
    • 

  • Prevalidation fails. Error message describes a different endpoint. Its text mentions only_user_info, which this workflow never reads. It looks copied from another workflow.
    • 

  • Only correo is validated. correoNuevo is not checked for format or against Authorized domains.
    • 

  • If valid domains. Get row(s) has alwaysOutputData on, so an unknown domain yields one empty item instead of none. The check is therefore "the first item has at least one key", not "there are items".
    • 

  • get User details error handling. The node uses onError: continueErrorOutput, so failures leave through its second output straight to Not found field false and debug info. The If get user details not contains error message → If not found path on the first output checks for the same failure and is probably never taken on its false side; it looks like a leftover from before the error output was used.
    • 

  • Wait → HTTP Request runs after the caller has its answer. The alias removal is not reflected in the response and its failure is swallowed (onError: continueRegularOutput, one retry after 5 s). A failed cleanup leaves the old address as an alias, with nothing reported.
    • 

  • Typos that are part of the output. Not found field Return message-1 writes debug.mesage while its sibling writes debug.message. Node names Cambier Nombre / Cambier Apellido are spelled that way in n8n.
    • 



Who uses it


Not recorded in the workflow. The pinned test request was made with curl, which says nothing about the real caller. To be filled in.

Trigger


POST /webhook/workspace/user/suspend on the n8n instance (Webhook node, path workspace/user/suspend).


Authentication is header auth, using the credential Header Auth Bearer token n8n.workspace.


The response is the output of whichever node runs last (responseMode: lastNode, all entries).


Request body


The body schema is not declared in the workflow; this is inferred from the expressions that read $json.body.*.






Field
Required
Used for





correo
Yes
Email of the account to suspend. Must look like an email and its domain must be in the Authorized domains data table.





What it does


    

  1. Pre-validation. Body parameters pre-validation checks correo against an email regex. Get row(s) looks up the domain of correo in the Authorized domains data table, and If valid domains passes only if a row came back. Either failure ends in Prevalidation fails. Error message.
    2. 

  2. Look up the user. get User details fetches the user by correo (retries once after 2 s). If the lookup fails, the workflow ends in Not found field false and debug info or Not found field Return message-1.
    3. 

  3. Suspend. Suspender Cuenta sends PUT https://admin.googleapis.com/admin/directory/v1/users/{correo} with suspended set to true.
    4.

Tricky nodes


    

  • Suspender Cuenta is a raw HTTP call, not the Google Workspace Admin node. It sends suspended as the string "true" in the body parameters and relies on Google accepting it.
    • 

  • No check for the account's current state. An account that is already suspended is sent the same PUT again.
    • 

  • Errors come back as normal responses. Validation and not-found branches finish successfully, so the caller has to read the body (error, not_found) to know nothing was suspended.
    • 

  • Prevalidation fails. Error message describes a different endpoint. Its text mentions only_user_info, which this workflow never reads.
    • 

  • If valid domains. Get row(s) has alwaysOutputData on, so an unknown domain yields one empty item. The check is "the first item has at least one key".
    • 

  • get User details error handling. Failures leave through the node's error output straight to Not found field false and debug info. The If get user details not contains error message → If not found path on the first output is probably never taken on its false side.
    • 

  • debug.mesage typo. Not found field Return message-1 writes debug.mesage; its sibling writes debug.message.
    • 



Who uses it


Not recorded in the workflow. To be filled in.

Workspaces User Discovery v1.4

            
Returns what a Google Workspace user has and belongs to: basic account details and, on request, admin details, shared drives, groups, delegated mailboxes, Chat spaces and Drive files. It is called over a webhook and answers with one combined object.

          


          

            

              

                Trigger
                What it does
                Credentials
                Tricky nodes
                Who uses it
              

              

                


Draft note. At import the editor showed unpublished changes (draft last saved 2026-09-23, published version from 2026-03-28). A comparison of the two versions in n8n found no difference in nodes or connections apart from canvas positions, so this JSON should behave like the published version.




Trigger


POST /webhook/workspace/user/details on the n8n instance (Webhook node, path workspace/user/details).


Authentication is header auth, using the credential Header Auth Bearer token n8n.workspace.


The response is the output of whichever node runs last (responseMode: lastNode, all entries).


Request body


The body schema is not declared in the workflow; this is inferred from the expressions that read $json.body.*.






Field
Required
Used for





correo
Yes
Email of the user to look up. Must look like an email and its domain must be in the Authorized domains data table.




moreDetails
No
true adds admin flags, alternate emails and recovery contact details.




sharedDrives
No
true adds the shared drives the user can see.




groups
No
true adds the groups the user belongs to.




delegated
No
true adds the mailboxes delegated to the user.




spaces
No
true adds the user's Chat spaces and group chats.




driveFiles
No
true adds the three Drive file sections: sharedToUser, sharedByUser and inSharedDrivesOwnedByUser.





The six flags are compared strictly with the boolean true. A missing flag, "true" as a string, or 1 all count as off.


What it does


    

  1. Pre-validation. Body parameters pre-validation checks correo against an email regex. Get row(s) looks up the domain in the Authorized domains data table, and If valid domains passes only if a row came back. Either failure ends in Prevalidation fails. Error message.
    2. 

  2. Look up the user. get User details fetches the user by correo (retries once). If the lookup fails, the workflow ends in Not found field false and debug info or Not found field Return message-1.
    3. 

  3. Basic details, always. Edit Fields Return Minimal User Details keeps email, firstName, lastName, orgUnitPath, suspended, archived, isEnrolledIn2Sv.
    4. 

  4. Optional sections. Set user email field for more details sets impersonate_email to the user's address and fans out to six If nodes, one per flag:
      

    • moreDetails — Edit Fields User Details builds moreDetails.*: workspaces_id, kind, isAdmin, isDelegatedAdmin, suspended, archived, emails, recoveryEmail, recoveryPhone.
      • 

    • sharedDrives — Direct Shared drives lists shared drives with the service account; Aggregate collects them under saredDrives.
      • 

    • groups — Get user groups calls GET https://admin.googleapis.com/admin/directory/v1/groups?userKey={email}.
      • 

    • delegated — Get rows on Cache Cuentas Delegadas reads the Cuentas delegadas data table for rows where delegateEmail is the user; the mailboxes are collected under delegatedEmails.
      • 

    • spaces — Listar Chats calls GET https://chat.googleapis.com/v1/spaces filtered to spaces and group chats; Split Out, Chats (Espacios) and Aggregate spaces reduce them to a spaces list.
      • 

    • driveFiles — get all files-folders lists every non-trashed file and folder with all fields, and Edit Fields trims each one. Three results come out of it:
        

      • sharedToUser: shared with the user and not owned by them (Filter shared_with_me).
        • 

      • sharedByUser: owned by the user and shared, with permissions (Owned and shared by User).
        • 

      • inSharedDrivesOwnedByUser: owned by the user and sitting in a shared drive, with the drive's name added (En unidad compartida propiedad del usuario → Get shared drive names → Merge1).
        • 

      

      • 

    

    5. 

  5. Combine. Merge joins its nine inputs by position into one item, which is the webhook response.
    6. 



Responses






Situation
What the caller gets





User found
One object with the basic details plus a key for each section requested.




Validation failed
error with the text built by Prevalidation fails. Error message.




User lookup failed
not_found, correo and the debug.* fields from the Not found… node that ran.

It also reads two n8n data tables: Authorized domains (ID rkrHk1gMjSJ6pTwu) and Cuentas delegadas (ID 0bQyjaMLc5SjLjci), the second kept up to date by Actualizar tabla cuentas delegadas.


Failed executions are reported by Notificación de errores, set as this workflow's error workflow in n8n.


Tricky nodes


    

  • impersonate_email decides whose data the service account sees. The service-account nodes carry no user in their own parameters; they appear to act as whoever impersonate_email names. Set user email field for more details sets it to the user being looked up, and Agregar impersonate email switches it to n8n.workspace@evdsky.com so that Get shared drive names can read drive names with domain admin access. The credential's configuration is not part of the export, so this mechanism is inferred from the node names.
    • 

  • Merge — nine inputs, most of them optional. Inputs are, in order: basic details, moreDetails, saredDrives, groups, delegatedEmails, spaces, sharedToUser, sharedByUser, inSharedDrivesOwnedByUser. Branches whose flag is off never deliver anything, and the workflow relies on Merge still running with the inputs that did arrive.
    • 

  • get all files-folders is the slow part. It requests every non-trashed file with fields: *, and the webhook does not answer until it finishes. It continues on error, so a failed listing returns a response without the three file sections instead of an error.
    • 

  • Impersonate Workspade admin does not impersonate anything. It is a Set node that copies file fields (as strings) before Merge1.
    • 

  • Get user groups returns at most 200 groups and does not follow nextPageToken.
    • 

  • Prevalidation fails. Error message describes the wrong body. It mentions only_user_info, which this workflow never reads, and none of the six real flags.
    • 

  • If valid domains. Get row(s) has alwaysOutputData on, so an unknown domain yields one empty item. The check is "the first item has at least one key".
    • 

  • get User details error handling. Failures leave through the node's error output straight to Not found field false and debug info. The If get user details not contains error message → If not found path on the first output is probably never taken on its false side.
    • 

  • Typos that are part of the output. The shared drives key is saredDrives, Not found field Return message-1 writes debug.mesage, and isEnrolledIn2Sv is returned as a string.
    • 

  • The flag If nodes are named inconsistently. If moreDetails True1 and plain If (the driveFiles check) sit alongside If groups True, If delegated True, If spaces True and If sharedDrives True.
    • 



Who uses it


Not recorded in the workflow. The Sticky Note on the canvas describes the intent: asking n8n which groups a person is in, what privileges they have in the Workspace, and which shared drives and delegated mailboxes they have. To be filled in.

Actualizar campo Comunidad WhatsApp auto COL

            
Keeps a HighLevel contact field in step with membership of the Colombia WhatsApp announcements group. When someone joins or leaves the group, it finds the matching contact in the Colombia HighLevel account by phone number and sets the "Grupo de avisos WhatsApp" custom field to Ingresado or Retirado.

          


          

            

              

                Trigger
                What it does
                Credentials
                Tricky nodes
                Who uses it
              

              

                
Trigger


POST /webhook/waha/participants on the n8n instance (Webhook node, path waha/participants).


Authentication is header auth, using the credential Header Auth n8n.highlevel.


The response is the output of whichever node runs last (responseMode: lastNode, all entries).


Request body


The body schema is not declared in the workflow; this is inferred from the expressions that read body.*. The caller is WAHA (the WhatsApp HTTP API), which sends its group-participants event; only these fields are read.






Field
Required
Used for





session
Yes
WAHA session name, used for the two lookups back into WAHA.




payload.type
Yes
Event type. Only values containing join or leave are processed.




payload.participants
Yes
Participants affected by the event. Only the first entry's id is used.




payload.group.id
Yes
WhatsApp id of the group the event happened in.





What it does


    

  1. Filter the event. If continues only when payload.type contains join or leave.
    2. 

  2. Look up the person. Get contact basic info asks WAHA for the first participant's contact, and Edit Fields1 keeps the phone number as +{number} together with the event type.
    3. 

  3. Check the group. Get the group. asks WAHA for the group, and If1 continues only if the group's subject contains "Colombia". Otherwise Stop and Error1 fails the execution with "Grupo no es Anuncios Colombia".
    4. 

  4. Find the custom field. Get row(s) reads the CustomFieldsHighLevel data table for the field named "Grupo de avisos WhatsApp" in the sede named by the last word of the group's subject.
    5. 

  5. Find the contact. Merge joins the person and the field, and Search contact in Highlevel searches the Colombia account for a contact whose phone contains the number. If none is found, Stop and Error fails the execution with "No found".
    6. 

  6. Update the field. Switch routes join to Edit Fields (Ingresado) and leave to Edit Fields2 (Retirado), and Update Grupo Avisos sends PUT https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/contacts/{contactId} with the new value.
    7. 



Responses






Situation
What the caller gets





Field updated
The HighLevel response to the contact update.




Event is not a join or leave
n8n's default response; the workflow ends at If.




Group is not a Colombia group, or no contact has that phone
n8n's error response, because a Stop and Error node fails the execution.

Bearer Auth Colombia Highlevel
httpBearerAuth
PyXklTRTJY2dAosR

It reads the n8n data table CustomFieldsHighLevel (ID dnPzVbYwHPI3hP3B), which is filled by Actualizar tabla cache custom fields highlevel.


It needs the community node @devlikeapro/n8n-nodes-waha installed on the instance.


Failed executions are reported by Notificación de errores (ID RFQhLaxt4mH5fioB), set as this workflow's error workflow in n8n.


Tricky nodes


    

  • Normal events end as errors. Someone joining a non-Colombia group, or a participant who is not a HighLevel contact, fails the execution through Stop and Error. Each of those triggers an error email.
    • 

  • Get row(s) derives the sede from the group's name. It takes the last word of the WhatsApp group subject and matches it against the sede column. Renaming the group changes which row, if any, is found.
    • 

  • If1 only checks for the word "Colombia", and both HighLevel nodes use the Colombia credential. The workflow is Colombia-only even though step 4 looks the sede up generically.
    • 

  • Search contact in Highlevel matches by "phone contains". A short or partial number could match the wrong contact; only the first result is used.
    • 

  • Only the first participant is handled. An event that adds or removes several people updates one contact.
    • 

  • Merge pairs by position the person (input 1) with the custom-field row (input 2), so it relies on each branch producing exactly one item.
    • 

  • Error outputs are not connected. Search contact in Highlevel and Update Grupo Avisos use onError: continueErrorOutput, so a failed HighLevel call ends that branch without an error email.
    • 



Who uses it


WAHA calls it automatically on WhatsApp group membership events. The result is used by whoever works with the Colombia HighLevel account. To be filled in.

Actualizar tabla cache custom fields highlevel

            
Rebuilds the n8n data table CustomFieldsHighLevel, a cache of every custom field in every HighLevel account. For each account it fetches the custom fields, then replaces the table's contents with the fresh list.

          


          

            

              

                Trigger
                What it does
                Credentials
                Tricky nodes
                Who uses it
              

              

                
Trigger


    

  • Schedule Trigger: the rule is left at its defaults (interval: [{}]), which in n8n means once a day at midnight, in the instance's timezone.
    • 

  • When clicking ‘Execute workflow’: manual run from the editor.
    • 

  • Webhook: a POST webhook with header auth is on the canvas but disabled, so it exposes no endpoint.
    • 



What it does


    

  1. Read the accounts. Get row(s) tabla LocationIDs reads the data table HighLevel_Location_IDs: one row per account with its sede name and locationId.
    2. 

  2. Route by account. Switch sends each row to the branch for its sede. There are 16 branches: Global, Iniciados, CLEV and the 13 sedes (Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Cuenca, España, Italia, México, Online, Perú, Quito, Uruguay and Venezuela).
    3. 

  3. Fetch the custom fields. Each branch has its own Get Custom Fields <account> node calling GET https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/locations/{locationId}/customFields with that account's credential.
    4. 

  4. Label and flatten. Each branch's Edit Fields… node adds locationName, and its Split Out… node produces one item per custom field.
    5. 

  5. Combine. Merge, Merge1 and Merge2 append all branches into one list, and New fields reduces each item to customFieldName, customFieldId, customFieldFieldKey, sede and locationId.
    6. 

  6. Replace the table. Obtener filas exisitentes reads the current rows of CustomFieldsHighLevel, Borrar filas existentes deletes them, and once that has finished Merge3 lets the new list through to Escribir filas nuevas, which inserts it.
    7.

It reads the data table HighLevel_Location_IDs (ID p5K85zArH4y1XQ61) and rewrites CustomFieldsHighLevel (ID dnPzVbYwHPI3hP3B).


Failed executions are reported by Notificación de errores (ID RFQhLaxt4mH5fioB), set as this workflow's error workflow in n8n.


Tricky nodes


    

  • One branch per account exists because each HighLevel account has its own token. n8n cannot pick a credential from data, so Switch routes each row to a node that has the right credential attached. Adding an account means adding a Switch rule, a credential and a four-node branch.
    • 

  • Escribir filas nuevas writes the field id into customFieldKey. Both the customFieldKey and customFieldId columns are filled from customFieldId; the real key (customFieldFieldKey) is computed by New fields but never written. Workflows that read customFieldKey from this table get the id instead.
    • 

  • The table is emptied before it is refilled. If the insert fails after Borrar filas existentes has run, the cache is left empty until the next run, and the workflows that read it find no fields.
    • 

  • A failed account stops the whole run. The Get Custom Fields… nodes have no error handling, so one bad token fails the execution before the table is touched.
    • 

  • Merge3 is only there for ordering. It waits for the delete branch and then passes on its second input, the new rows.
    • 

  • Borrar filas existentes has no column name in its filter. The condition only carries the value $json.id and relies on the node's default key.
    • 

  • Switch matches sede names exactly, accents included (México, Perú, España). Other workflows in this area spell some of them without accents.
    • 



Who uses it


No person calls it in normal operation; it runs on its schedule. Its output, the CustomFieldsHighLevel table, is read by Actualizar campo Comunidad WhatsApp auto COL and Upsert Contacts from Iniciados to Sedes.

Authentication is header auth, using the credential Header Auth n8n.highlevel.

What it does


    

  1. Read the contact. Search for a contact id calls POST https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/contacts/search for the contact with that id in that location.
    2. 

  2. Update the cache. Update row(s) finds the row of Cache contactos Iniciados SKY whose contactIdIniciados equals the contact's id and overwrites firstName, lastName, phone, email, sede, estadoDelIniciado, circulo and grupoSky.

Failed executions are reported by Notificación de errores (ID RFQhLaxt4mH5fioB), set as this workflow's error workflow in n8n.


Tricky nodes


    

  • Update row(s) reads custom fields by position. estadoDelIniciado is customFields[0], grupoSky is [1], sede is [2] and circulo is [3]. HighLevel does not promise that order; a contact with a missing or extra custom field would put values in the wrong columns.
    • 

  • It only updates, never inserts. A contact that is not already in the cache table is not added; the update matches nothing and nothing is reported.
    • 

  • The webhook body is trusted for the location. The search uses location.id from the request with the Iniciados credential, so a call for a contact in another account returns nothing.
    • 

  • "PI" in the name is not explained anywhere in the workflow.
    • 



Who uses it


A HighLevel workflow in the Iniciados account calls it when a contact is updated. The cache it maintains is read by Upsert Contacts from Iniciados to Sedes. To be filled in: which HighLevel workflow.

Notificación de errores

            
Sends an email whenever another workflow fails. It is the shared error handler for the HighLevel workflows, not something that is called directly. Separate workflows with the same name do the same job for the Google Workspace and CLEV areas.

          


          

            

              

                Trigger
                What it does
                Credentials

Trigger


Error Trigger. n8n runs this workflow when a workflow that names it as its error workflow fails.


At import, seven published workflows had it set as their error workflow in their n8n settings: Actualizar campo Comunidad WhatsApp auto COL, Actualizar tabla cache custom fields highlevel, Actualizar tabla cache iniciados - iniciado actualizado desde PI, Upsert Contacts from Iniciados to Sedes, Sub. Upsert contact by email multi credential Iniciados Sedes, Sub. Search all contacts by Sede Location ID multi credential and Copia contacto CRM a teléfono. Two had none: Search contact email multi credential and test webhook events Iniciados.


What it does


    

  1. Error Trigger receives the failed execution's details.
    2. 

  2. Send email sends a plain-text email from n8n@evdsky.com to servidores@evdsky.com with the subject Error en workflow n8n.highlevel: {workflow name}. The body lists the workflow name, execution URL, last node executed, execution mode, execution ID, error message and stack trace.
    3.

Whoever reads servidores@evdsky.com. Returns every contact of one sede's HighLevel account. It is a sub-workflow: other workflows call it, it has no webhook or schedule. Only the Argentina and Chile branches are active.

Trigger


When Executed by Another Workflow (Execute Workflow Trigger) with two inputs: sede and locationIdSede. None of the other imported workflows calls it.


What it does


    

  1. Route by sede. Switch has one output per sede, each leading to a Get All Contacts <sede> node with that sede's credential.
    2. 

  2. Fetch all contacts. The node calls GET https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/contacts/?locationId={locationIdSede}&limit=100 and follows HighLevel's startAfter / startAfterId cursor until there are no more pages.
    3. 

  3. Return. Merge appends the Argentina and Chile results.
    4.

Tricky nodes

Creates or updates one contact in a sede's HighLevel account, matched by email, and sets its "iniciado" custom fields. It is a sub-workflow: other workflows call it, it has no webhook or schedule.

Trigger


When Executed by Another Workflow (Execute Workflow Trigger). At import the only caller is Upsert Contacts from Iniciados to Sedes.


It declares 16 inputs: sede, locationIdSede, email, firstName, lastName, estadoDelIniciado, estadoDelIniciadoCustomFieldIdSede, estadoDelIniciadoCustomFieldKeySede, circulo, circuloCustomFieldIdSede, circuloCustomFieldKeySede, grupoSky, grupoSkyCustomFieldIdSede, grupoSkyCustomFielKeySede, sedeCustomFieldIdSede and sedeCustomFieldKeySede.


What it does


    

  1. Route by sede. Switch sends the item to one of 13 outputs: Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Cuenca, España, Italia, México, Online, Perú, Quito, Uruguay and Venezuela.

Tricky nodes


    

  • One node per sede exists because each HighLevel account has its own token. n8n cannot pick a credential from data, so Switch routes to the node that has the right credential attached. All 13 upsert nodes are otherwise the same; a change to the request body has to be made 13 times.
    • 

  • Two custom fields send the id as the key. In the request body, the grupo SKY and sede fields use …CustomFieldIdSede for both id and key, while estado and círculo use the separate …KeySede input. The inputs grupoSkyCustomFielKeySede and sedeCustomFieldKeySede are declared but never used.
    • 

  • Every upsert continues on error (onError: continueRegularOutput). A rejected upsert returns its error as ordinary data, the run finishes successfully and no error email is sent.
    • 

  • Input names are inconsistent: grupoSkyCustomFielKeySede is missing a d. The caller has to use the same spelling.
    • 

  • Switch matches sede exactly, accents included. A sede value with no matching rule is dropped silently.
    • 

  • Merge is split in two (10 inputs and 4 inputs) only because of how many inputs one node can take.
    • 



Who uses it


Upsert Contacts from Iniciados to Sedes.

Upsert Contacts from Iniciados to Sedes

            
Copies the "iniciados" from the cache table into HighLevel: every cached person is upserted into the Global account and, through a sub-workflow, into the account of their sede. It runs on a schedule.

          


          

            

              

                Trigger
                What it does
                Credentials
                Tricky nodes
                Who uses it
              

              

                


Draft note. At import the editor showed unpublished changes (draft last saved 2026-04-10, published version from 2026-03-31). The JSON in this folder and this document are the published (live) version. The unpublished draft is a rework of the custom-field handling:


    

  • It replaces Switch and Edit Fields1, Edit Fields3, Edit Fields4 with Switch Custom Fields, Estado del Iniciado IDs, Grupo SKY IDs, Círculo IDs, a new Sede IDs branch and Merge4, so the sede custom field is handled too.
    • 

  • Call 'Upsert contact by email multi credential' maps all 16 sub-workflow inputs explicitly; in the published version the mapping is empty.
    • 

  • Upsert contacts Global also sends each custom field's key.
    • 

  • Edit Fields2 no longer sets the four …CustomFielIdSede fields.
    • 





Trigger


    

  • Schedule Trigger: the rule is left at its defaults (interval: [{}]), which in n8n means once a day at midnight, in the instance's timezone.
    • 

  • When clicking ‘Execute workflow’: manual run from the editor.
    • 



There is no webhook.


What it does


    

  1. Read three tables, in parallel:
      

    • Get Iniciados SKY reads Cache contactos Iniciados SKY: one row per person with name, email, phone, sede, estado, círculo and grupo SKY.
      • 

    • Get Location IDs sedes reads the location-id table: sede → locationId.
      • 

    • Get Custon Field Sedes reads CustomFieldsHighLevel: the custom fields of every account.
      • 

    

    2. 

  2. Attach the sede's location. Edit Fields2 and Edit Fields shape the two inputs, and Merge adds locationIdSede to each person by matching on sede.
    3. 

  3. Attach the sede's custom-field ids. Switch splits the custom-field rows into "Estado del Iniciado", "Grupo SKY" and "Círculo"; Edit Fields1, Edit Fields3 and Edit Fields4 rename their id, key and name; and Merge1, Merge2, Merge3 add each set to the person, again matching on sede.
    4. 

  4. Upsert into the sede account. Call 'Upsert contact by email multi credential' runs the sub-workflow Sub. Upsert contact by email multi credential Iniciados Sedes and waits for it.
    5. 

  5. Upsert into the Global account. In parallel, Upsert contacts Global calls POST https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/contacts/upsert with the person's name, email, estado, círculo and grupo SKY.
    6. 



Credentials






Credential
Type
ID
Used by





Bearer Auth Global Highlevel
httpBearerAuth
O5VIrmRZ8U44X95T
Upsert contacts Global





It reads three n8n data tables: Cache contactos Iniciados SKY (ID IsF4IohkX1358wkI), the location-id table (ID p5K85zArH4y1XQ61) and CustomFieldsHighLevel (ID dnPzVbYwHPI3hP3B).


The sede accounts are written through the sub-workflow, which holds their 13 credentials.


Failed executions are reported by Notificación de errores (ID RFQhLaxt4mH5fioB), set as this workflow's error workflow in n8n.


Tricky nodes


    

  • The published call to the sub-workflow maps no inputs. Call 'Upsert contact by email multi credential' has an empty mapping, while the sub-workflow expects 16 named inputs. Whether the sede upserts receive any data in the published version has not been checked against an execution; the draft fills the mapping in, which suggests they did not.
    • 

  • Upsert contacts Global hard-codes the Global account. The location id and the three custom-field ids are written into the request body instead of coming from the tables.
    • 

  • Everyone is upserted on every run. There is no "changed since" filter, so each run sends one Global request per cached person plus one sub-workflow call.
    • 

  • Switch rule for Círculo is 'Círculo' || 'Circulo', which always evaluates to 'Círculo'. A field named Circulo without the accent does not match.
    • 

  • The merges enrich by sede and keep all matches. A sede with two custom fields of the same name would duplicate every person in that sede.
    • 

  • Field names are inconsistent. Edit Fields2 writes …CustomFielIdSede (missing d), the later nodes write …CustomFieldIdSede, and the sub-workflow expects grupoSkyCustomFielKeySede.
    • 

  • The sede values must match across three tables and the sub-workflow's Switch, accents included.
    • 



Who uses it


No person calls it in normal operation; it runs on its schedule. It depends on Actualizar tabla cache iniciados - iniciado actualizado desde PI and Actualizar tabla cache custom fields highlevel keeping its input tables current.
